(2) The cookie banner on line 111 links to /gizlilik-kvkk.html, Turkey's KVKK data-protection law. EN needs an English privacy/cookie notice written around GDPR in general terms. (3) The Turkish date '19 Eylül 2026' on line 75 and the Turkish kicker and tags 'Yıldız Günlüğü', 'Temeller' and 'Doğum Haritası' (lines 73-76). rationale: This is a short static explainer: about 505 words of article prose plus FAQ, about 640 visible words in total. It has no tool and no backend calls, and the only Turkish string in inline JS is 'Hesabım' on line 70. Translating it would therefore be trivial and low-risk; the real work is shared chrome (an EN menu without Asterna, PWA or report links, and an EN cookie notice). The trouble is SEO and unique value. 'Moon sign' is a large English topic, but the SERP is saturated by high-authority sites: cafeastrology, astrology.com, astro-seek, Co-Star/CHANI, Allure, Cosmopolitan, Refinery29, timeanddate-style calculators. Most of that demand is really 'what is my moon sign', which a calculator satisfies, not a 500-word definition. A generic explainer on a new EN subfolder with no English backlinks has little chance of ranking or bringing visitors, and since we cannot sell the Turkish reports, it would earn nothing on its own. Better plan: build a client-side EN Moon Sign Calculator for phase 1, reusing astronomy-engine, which already runs client-side on lilith-burcu-hesaplama.html, zaman-makinesi.html and others. Take the date, an optional time and a timezone/UTC offset, warn when the Moon changes sign that day, and output fixed English sign names plus a short English blurb per sign. This article's content (Sun/Moon/Rising difference, why birth time matters, FAQ) can serve as that calculator's explanatory section or as a phase-2 supporting article linked from it. Do not spend a phase-1 slot on it as a standalone page.
